verdict: Both are excellent everyday assistants and cost the same. ChatGPT does more kinds of things in one app, including images and voice. Claude is the stronger pick for careful writing, long documents and code.
pickA: You want one app that also makes images and talks by voice
You like having the widest choice of add-ons and custom assistants
People around you already use it and share tips
pickB: Most of your work is writing, editing or reading long reports
You want help with code, or plan to use Claude Code
You prefer answers that are careful and say when they are unsure
both: Many people keep both free plans and pay for the one they open more often.

verdict: ChatGPT is the better general assistant on its own. Gemini wins if your email, files and calendar already live in Google, because it can read them and it is included in cheaper Google plans.
pickA: You want the strongest all-round answers for writing and problem solving
You do not use Gmail or Google Docs much
You want image creation and voice chat in the same place
pickB: Your mail and documents are in Gmail, Docs and Drive
You want a capable assistant at a lower monthly price
You often need fresh answers backed by Google Search

verdict: Claude is the better writer and coder. Gemini is the better helper inside Google's apps and the cheaper way to get a paid plan.
pickA: You write, edit or analyse long documents
You code or want an AI to work on a software project
Quality of the answer matters more than price
pickB: You want AI inside Gmail, Docs and Drive
You need a low-cost paid plan
You want answers that draw on Google Search

verdict: These are different tools. ChatGPT is for creating and thinking things through. Perplexity is for looking things up, with links to the sources so you can check them.
pickA: You want to write, rewrite, plan or brainstorm
You want to upload a file and work on it
You need images or voice chat
pickB: You are researching a question and want to see where the answer came from
You compare products or prices before buying
You want a quick, sourced summary of recent news
both: A common setup is Perplexity for finding facts and ChatGPT or Claude for turning them into a text.

verdict: Copilot is the convenient choice if you live in Word, Excel and Outlook, because it works inside them with a Microsoft 365 plan. As a standalone assistant, ChatGPT is more capable and more flexible.
pickA: You want the best assistant regardless of which office software you use
You want images, voice chat and custom assistants
You do not pay for Microsoft 365
pickB: Your work happens in Word, Excel, Outlook or Teams
You already pay for Microsoft 365
You want quick answers from the Windows taskbar or Edge

verdict: Both are for people who write code. GitHub Copilot is the cheaper helper that lives inside the editor you already use. Cursor is a whole editor built around AI and goes further when you want an agent to change many files.
pickA: You want the AI to plan and make changes across a whole project
You are happy to switch to a new code editor
You are willing to pay more for heavier use
pickB: You want to keep VS Code or your current editor
You mostly want suggestions as you type and a chat for questions
You want the lowest price, or a useful free plan

verdict: Both build a working website or app from a description, with no coding. Lovable is the gentler start for a complete beginner. Bolt.new shows more of the code and hosts the result for you, which helps if a developer will take over later.
pickA: You have never built a website and want the simplest path
You want a finished-looking result from a short description
You are making a landing page, a prototype or a small internal tool
pickB: You want a monthly free allowance to experiment with
You or a colleague can read code and want to see it
You want to host the result with one click
both: With either one, have someone check the app for security problems before real customer data goes into it.

verdict: Midjourney makes the most artistic, polished pictures but has no free plan. Ideogram is free to start and is the one to use when the picture must contain readable text, such as a poster or logo.
pickA: You want striking artwork, illustrations or concept images
Style and mood matter more than exact wording in the picture
You are fine paying from the first day
pickB: You need correct lettering in a poster, logo or social graphic
You want to try for free first
You need the same character across several images

verdict: Both connect your apps so routine work happens by itself. Zapier is easier to learn and connects to the most apps. Make is cheaper for the same amount of work and more flexible, but takes longer to learn.
pickA: You are new to automation and want it working in minutes
You need a less common app that others may not support
You only automate a handful of simple tasks
pickB: You run many automations and want to keep the cost down
Your flows have several branches and conditions
You are comfortable spending time to learn a visual builder

verdict: Gamma is the fastest way from an outline to a finished slide deck. Canva is a full design tool: better when you also need social posts, flyers and brand graphics, and when you want to control the layout yourself.
pickA: You need a presentation quickly and care more about content than design
You start from notes, an outline or a PDF
You want to export to PowerPoint or Google Slides
pickB: You design many kinds of things, not only slides
You want templates and to move every element yourself
Your team already keeps its brand colours and logos in Canva

verdict: Both turn a short description into a full song with vocals. Suno is the practical choice today: Udio no longer lets you download songs, so they can only be played on Udio.
pickA: You want to download the song and use it in a video or at an event
You want the larger free daily allowance
You may need commercial rights later, on a paid plan
pickB: You only want to listen and share inside Udio
You like extending and remixing songs you made there
You want to compare how the two sound on the same idea

verdict: Both record a meeting, write the transcript and send a summary. Otter is simple and good for one person. Fireflies suits a team that wants to search past meetings and share what was decided.
pickA: You mainly want transcripts and summaries for yourself
You want a generous free allowance of meeting minutes
You want the simplest setup
pickB: A team needs to search past meetings and share action items
You want action items sent to the team after each call
You are fine with a bot joining the call
both: Whichever you use, tell the other people that the meeting is being recorded.

verdict: Both make short video clips from text or a picture. Runway is also an editor, so you can remove objects and add sound in the same place. Kling AI focuses on realistic clips and has a free plan to try it.
pickA: You want to edit video as well as generate it
You need to remove or replace things in existing footage
You want music, voice and sound effects in one tool
pickB: You mainly want realistic-looking clips
You want to try on a free plan first
You want to copy a person's movement onto a character

verdict: Grammarly corrects your writing as you type, in almost every app. QuillBot is for rewording and summarising text you paste in. They solve different problems and many people use both.
pickA: You want mistakes fixed while you write emails and documents
You want help with tone: more polite, more confident, shorter
You want it to work everywhere without copying text around
pickB: You want to say the same thing in different words
You want an article summarised into key points
You need citations generated for school work

verdict: Both make a video of a lifelike presenter reading your script. HeyGen is stronger for marketing and for translating videos with matching lip movement. Synthesia is built for company training and gives more free minutes.
pickA: You make sales, marketing or social videos
You want to translate an existing video into other languages
You want a digital version of yourself as the presenter
pickB: You make training or explainer videos for a company
You want to turn documents or slides into video
You want more free video minutes each month
